record.paper_title: The Feynman integral path a Henstock integral: a survey and open problems
record.context_brief: Cone and supremum approach in a Banach space
record.original_question: Let g0(x,N,I[N]) be the free-particle Fresnel integrand and let β(x,N,I[N]) be the positive integrable majorant required by bounded convergence for Henstock integration on R^T. Suppose E is a Banach space equipped with a cone P that defines a partial order, and that both |g0| and β belong to E. In the case where β ≤ |g0| for every γ0-fine associated triple (equivalently, |g0|−β ∈ P), can one introduce a suitable supremum notion in E and use it to obtain the contradiction needed to analyze whether the Henstock path integral can be exchanged with the perturbation series?

evidence.quote: In the case that, |g0|−β ∈ P for each γ0−fine (x, N, I[N]) implies that β ≤ |g0|, for every γ0−fine (x, N, I[N]), here we need to introduce the supremum in Banach spaces in order to give a contradiction.
This case is being analyzed with supremum concept.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer T and consider the space $\mathbb{R}^T$ of paths $x:\{1,\dots,T\}\to\mathbb{R}$. For a tagged division $(x,N,I[N])$ of $\mathbb{R}^T$ subordinate to a gauge $\gamma_0$ (a $\gamma_0$-fine associated triple in the sense of Henstock), let \[ g_0(x,N,I[N]) \] denote the free-particle Fresnel integrand used in the Henstock formulation of the Feynman path integral, and let \[ \beta(x,N,I[N]) \] be a positive integrable majorant required by the bounded convergence theorem for Henstock integration on $\mathbb{R}^T$.

Let $E$ be a Banach space equipped with a closed convex cone $P\subset E$ that induces a partial order $\le$ on $E$ via $u\le v\iff v-u\in P$. Assume that the maps $|g_0|$ and $\beta$, regarded as elements indexed by $\gamma_0$-fine associated triples, lie in $E$.

Consider the hypothesis
\[ |g_0(x,N,I[N])|-\beta(x,N,I[N])\in P \qquad\text{for every $\gamma_0$-fine }(x,N,I[N]), \]
equivalently $\beta\le|g_0|$ pointwise on the set of $\gamma_0$-fine associated triples.

Problem. Define a notion of supremum in the ordered Banach space $(E,P)$ (for instance, a least upper bound with respect to $\le$, possibly relative to a suitable subfamily) that is well adapted to the families $\{|g_0|\}$ and $\{\beta\}$, and use this supremum together with the hypothesis above to derive a contradiction with the bounded convergence requirement. Use the resulting argument to determine whether the Henstock path integral on $\mathbb{R}^T$ can be interchanged with the summation of the perturbation series defining the Feynman path integral.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a survey on Henstock-integral approaches to the Feynman path integral. No subsequent work resolving the proposed cone/supremum-in-Banach-space approach to interchange of Henstock path integration with the perturbation series has been located.

status_evidence.title: The Feynman integral path a Henstock integral: a survey and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on representing the Feynman path integral as a Henstock integral, including questions on bounded convergence and cone/supremum methods in Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem in a survey of open problems on the Henstock formulation of the Feynman path integral.
